verdict.summary: You can build this as a public GitHub App without GitHub approval. A basic production setup takes an estimated 3–6 hours of hands-on work. There is no required review wait unless you choose to publish a GitHub Marketplace listing. Each customer must install the App and select the repositories it can access.
verdict.activeEffort: Estimated 3–6 hours, mostly for secure token handling and webhook verification.
verdict.waitTime: None for public App installation. Marketplace publication has no fixed review time.
verdict.mainGate: Each customer must install the App and select repositories before the App can access their account.

recommendation.text: Use a public GitHub App with “Any account” installation. Create one App installation for each customer's account or organization. Use installation tokens for background repository work. Enable user authorization only when an action needs the user's own authority.

sources.quote: In general, GitHub Apps are preferred over OAuth apps.
If you want to access GitHub resources on behalf of a user or in an organization, or you anticipate a long-lived integration, we recommend building a GitHub App.
Under ‘Where can this GitHub App be installed?’, select Only on this account or Any account .

scopeTiers.text: Read repository files and basic repository details. This has the lowest access cost.

sources.quote: GitHub Apps don't have any permissions by default. When you register a GitHub App, you can select permissions for the app.

scopeTiers.need: Read the customer's selected repository files and metadata.
scopeTiers.scopes: Repository Contents: read; Repository Metadata: read

scopeTiers.text: Write files only in repositories the installer selected. Customers must approve the broader write permission during installation.

sources.quote: With a GitHub App, the user or organization owner who installed the app can decide what repositories the app can access.
GitHub Apps don't have any permissions by default. When you register a GitHub App, you can select permissions for the app.

scopeTiers.need: Create or edit ordinary repository files.

scopeTiers.text: Comment on issues and pull requests. Customers must approve write access for the relevant collaboration records.

sources.quote: The REST API reference documentation for each endpoint states whether the endpoint works with GitHub Apps and states what permissions are required

scopeTiers.need: Read and write issues or pull requests.
scopeTiers.scopes: Repository Issues: write; Repository Pull requests: write

scopeTiers.text: Edit GitHub Actions workflow files. This requires a separate permission beyond normal file writing.

sources.quote: If your app specifically needs to access or edit Actions files in the .github/workflows directory, request the ‘Workflows’ repository permission.

scopeTiers.scopes: Repository Contents: write; Repository Workflows: write

essentials.text: Installation tokens expire after one hour. User tokens expire after eight hours. User refresh tokens expire after six months. Store rotated refresh tokens atomically because using one invalidates the old tokens.

sources.quote: The installation access token will expire after 1 hour.
The user access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months.
Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work.

essentials.text: Use exact HTTPS callback URLs. GitHub allows up to 10 callbacks. Disable wildcard matching unless you control every matching host and path.

sources.quote: When wildcard matching is disabled, the redirect URL must exactly match the callback URL.
Enabling wildcard matching can expose your app to security risks, because it allows an attacker to send authorization codes to any subdomain or subdirectory of the callback URL.

essentials.text: Use a separate public development GitHub App with the same configuration. A draft Marketplace listing is visible only to the App owner. A user or organization can register up to 100 GitHub Apps.

sources.quote: we recommend configuring a separate development app, with the same configuration as your production app, and creating a draft GitHub Marketplace listing that you can use for testing.
A Marketplace listing in the draft state is only visible to the app's owner.
A user or organization can register up to 100 GitHub Apps, but there is no limit to how many GitHub Apps can be installed on an account.

essentials.text: Installation tokens have at least 5,000 REST requests per hour. Keep below 100 concurrent API requests. Content-generating requests are generally limited to 80 per minute and 500 per hour.

sources.quote: GitHub Apps authenticating with an installation access token use the installation's minimum rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
In general, no more than 80 content-generating requests per minute and no more than 500 content-generating requests per hour are allowed.

essentials.text: GitHub does not charge a separate fee to register or make a GitHub App public. Marketplace is optional. GitHub retains 5% of paid Marketplace transaction income after January 1, 2021.

sources.quote: Anyone can share their apps with other users for free on GitHub Marketplace but only apps owned by organizations can sell their app.
For transactions made after that date, only 5% is retained by GitHub.

essentials.text: Select “Any account” during registration so customers can install the App. Public installation does not require Marketplace approval. Keep the production App owned by your company organization.

sources.quote: Under ‘Where can this GitHub App be installed?’, select Only on this account or Any account .
This article applies to publishing apps in GitHub Marketplace only.

essentials.text: No review is required for public GitHub App installation. Marketplace review applies only if you request a Marketplace listing. GitHub gives no fixed Marketplace review time.

sources.quote: This article applies to publishing apps in GitHub Marketplace only.
An onboarding expert will reach out to you with additional information.

essentials.text: Keep keys and tokens in encrypted secret storage. Verify webhook signatures against the raw body using HMAC-SHA256. Use constant-time comparison. Protect user authorization with state and PKCE using S256.

sources.quote: Never hardcode a token into an application or push a token to any repository.
Validate incoming webhook payloads against the token, to verify that they are coming from GitHub and were not tampered with.
Never use a plain == operator.
Must be S256 - the plain code challenge method is not supported.

requests.text: Use a random state and PKCE challenge; requesting offline_access opts this sign-in into expiring tokens and refresh tokens.

sources.quote: GET https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize
scope string Context dependent A space-delimited list of scopes.

To test and gradually roll out support for expiring tokens, you can opt in to receive an expiring token and a refresh token for an individual sign-in by requesting the offline_access scope in addition to your other scopes.
code_challenge string Strongly recommended Used to secure the authentication flow with PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange).

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Codes expire in 10 minutes; include the original PKCE verifier.

sources.quote: POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token
client_id string Required The client ID you received from GitHub for your OAuth app.
code_verifier string Strongly recommended Used to secure the authentication flow with PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange). Required if code_challenge was sent during the user authorization.
The temporary code will expire after 10 minutes.

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens

requests.text: A refresh returns a new access token and refresh token; the old refresh token no longer works.

sources.quote: Make a POST request to this URL, along with the following query parameters: https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token
grant_type string Required. The value must be "refresh_token".
Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work.

requests.label: Refresh the access token

requests.text: Revalidate the signed-in user's identity after every authorization.

sources.quote:
Authorization: Bearer OAUTH-TOKEN
GET https://api.github.com/user
Every time you receive an access token, you should use the token to revalidate the user's identity.

requests.label: Check the connection

detail.text: Open your company organization's Settings, then Developer settings, then GitHub Apps. Register the production App under the company organization. This avoids depending on an employee account.

sources.quote: For an app owned by an organization: Click Your organizations . To the right of the organization, click Settings .

detail.text: Create a GitHub App and select “Any account” under installation availability. Enter your homepage, webhook URL, and callback URL. This lets each customer install the App into their own account or organization. If an action needs the user's own authority, enable GitHub App user authorization and protect that browser flow with state and PKCE. Do not use OAuth App `repo` or `workflow` scopes for GitHub App access; GitHub App permissions determine its access.

sources.quote: Under ‘Where can this GitHub App be installed?’, select Only on this account or Any account .

steps.title: Draft minimal permission rationale

detail.text: Use this text in your install screen and product disclosures. Keep only the permissions needed by enabled features. Add a separate explanation before requesting write access.

sources.quote: GitHub Apps don't have any permissions by default. When you register a GitHub App, you can select permissions for the app.
If your app specifically needs to access or edit Actions files in the .github/workflows directory, request the ‘Workflows’ repository permission.

steps.output:
Read-only rationale:
“GitHub Agent reads only files and metadata from repositories selected by the installer. It uses Contents: read and Metadata: read. It does not modify repositories.”

Write rationale:
“GitHub Agent creates requested file changes only in repositories selected by the installer. It uses Contents: write. Workflow-file changes require separate Workflows permission.”

detail.text: In the App's Permissions and events section, start with Contents: read and Metadata: read. Add write permissions only for shipped features. Add Workflows only when editing .github/workflows files.

sources.quote: GitHub Apps don't have any permissions by default. When you register a GitHub App, you can select permissions for the app.
If your app specifically needs to access or edit Actions files in the .github/workflows directory, request the ‘Workflows’ repository permission.

detail.text: Generate an App private key and place it in your secrets manager. Store the App ID, client secret, and webhook secret there too. Never send these values to browser code or source control.

sources.quote: Never hardcode a token into an application or push a token to any repository.

detail.text: Register a separate public development App with the same settings as production. Install it only into test accounts and test repositories. Do not use production credentials during development.

sources.quote: we recommend configuring a separate development app, with the same configuration as your production app, and creating a draft GitHub Marketplace listing that you can use for testing.

detail.text: Create a signed App JWT and exchange it with each installation ID for an installation token. Cache tokens safely and replace them before their one-hour expiry. Restrict tokens to the repositories needed for each job.

sources.quote: The installation access token will expire after 1 hour.
The installation access token cannot be granted permissions that the app was not granted.

detail.text: Verify X-Hub-Signature-256 against the unmodified request body before parsing or processing any webhook. Reject invalid signatures with a constant-time comparison. Queue valid deliveries for idempotent processing.

sources.quote: Validate incoming webhook payloads against the token, to verify that they are coming from GitHub and were not tampered with.
Never use a plain == operator.

detail.text: Do not submit for Marketplace review unless you need a Marketplace listing. Public GitHub App installation works without that review, and customers can install using your App's installation link. If you sell paid plans through Marketplace, the App must be organization-owned and meet Marketplace requirements. Paid plans also require publisher verification, at least 100 GitHub App installations, and handling Marketplace purchase, upgrade, downgrade, cancellation, and free-trial events.

sources.quote: This article applies to publishing apps in GitHub Marketplace only.

detail.text: Save one GitHub installation ID for each customer account in your database. On every job, load only that customer's installation ID. Never reuse an installation token across customers.

sources.quote: With a GitHub App, the user or organization owner who installed the app can decide what repositories the app can access.

detail.text: Queue repository jobs per installation. Limit concurrent calls and content-generating writes. Use exponential backoff and idempotency keys when GitHub returns rate-limit errors.

sources.quote: In general, no more than 80 content-generating requests per minute and no more than 500 content-generating requests per hour are allowed.

gotchas.text: Contents: write does not permit editing .github/workflows. Request Workflows permission when that feature is enabled.

sources.quote: If your app specifically needs to access or edit Actions files in the .github/workflows directory, request the ‘Workflows’ repository permission.

gotchas.text: Older Apps with one callback URL before August 3, 2026 may have wildcard matching enabled. Audit them before accepting customer authorizations.

sources.quote: Apps that had a single callback URL enabled prior to August 3, 2026 have wildcard matching enabled for that callback URL.

gotchas.text: User authorization is only needed when GitHub must apply the user's authority. Those requests can fail when either the user or the App lacks permission.

sources.quote: The success of an API request with a user access token depends on the user's permissions as well as the app's permissions.

gotchas.text: Marketplace paid plans require 100 GitHub App installations. This applies only when selling through GitHub Marketplace.

sources.quote: GitHub Apps should have a minimum of 100 installations.

whenBlocked.text: If an endpoint returns HTTP 403, check that endpoint's REST reference. Add only its required App permission, then ask customers to approve the updated installation permissions.

sources.quote: The REST API reference documentation for each endpoint states whether the endpoint works with GitHub Apps and states what permissions are required

whenBlocked.text: If a customer cannot install the App, ask their organization owner to approve the installation and select the required repositories.

sources.quote: With a GitHub App, the user or organization owner who installed the app can decide what repositories the app can access.

whenBlocked.text: If Marketplace publication stalls, first check technical, support, and security contact inboxes and spam. Then open a GitHub Support ticket with the listing URL and submission date.
